title: Spectrophotometry Method for Detection of Biochemical Parameters
author: Xiaohua Du
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6wchfaw

steps.title: Warm up the automatic analyser
steps.instruction: Turn on the automatic analyser and allow it to warm up for 00:15:00 to ensure accurate readings.

steps.title: Prepare samples and control solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the samples and a control solution (blank) consisting of the chemical solvent in which the solute is dissolved.

substeps.instruction: Load 1 milliliter (mL) of sample into the cuvette (note: test tubes have a volume of 5 mL).
Use different pipettes for each sample to prevent contamination.
Ensure the blank has the same volume as the solution to be analyzed and is kept in the same kind of container.

steps.title: Clean the cuvette
steps.instruction: Wipe the outside of the cuvette using a lint-free cloth to remove water droplets or dust particles to avoid interference.

steps.title: Set the analysis wavelength
steps.instruction: Select and set a single wavelength of light (monochromatic color) known to be absorbed by one of the chemicals suspected to be in the test solute, according to the spectrophotometer specifications.

steps.title: Calibrate the machine with the blank
steps.instruction: Calibrate the analyser using the blank solution to subtract its absorbance from subsequent samples.

substeps.instruction: Place the blank into the cuvette holder and close the lid.
Record the initial values, then move the needle to zero using the adjustment knob.
Remove the blank and verify the needle stays at 0.
Re-insert the blank to ensure the readout remains at 0.

steps.title: Measure experimental sample absorbance
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance (optical density) of the experimental sample.

substeps.instruction: Remove the blank and place the experimental sample upright into the designated groove.
Wait approximately 00:00:10 until the needle is steady or digital numbers change.
Record the % transmittance and/or absorbance (usually given as a decimal, e.g., 0.43).

steps.title: Perform spectral scan
steps.instruction: Repeat the absorbance readings at 25 nm intervals across the spectrum to detect other suspected chemicals and eliminate uncertainty.

steps.title: Calculate transmittance and absorbance
steps.instruction: If the analyser does not provide automatic output, calculate transmittance (T) and absorbance (A).

substeps.instruction: Calculate Transmittance: T = I/I0 (where I is sample intensity and I0 is blank intensity), expressed as a decimal or percentage.

steps.title: Generate and analyze absorbance spectrum
steps.instruction: Plot the data to identify the compounds and their proportions in the test substance.

substeps.instruction: Plot absorbance values on the vertical y-axis against the wavelengths on the horizontal x-axis.
Compare the resulting absorbance spectrum plot (peaks) to known plots of specific compounds to identify solutes or contaminants.
